name: Physics
description: Measurement, mechanics, heat, waves, optics, electricity, magnetism and modern physics for the Nigerian senior secondary curriculum, aligned to WAEC, NECO and JAMB requirements.

topics.name: Measurement and Units
topics.summary: Physical quantities, SI units, measuring instruments and how to report a measurement honestly.

subtopics.name: Fundamental and Derived Quantities
subtopics.summary: The base SI quantities and how every other physical quantity is built from them.

objectives.text: State the fundamental quantities and their SI units and symbols
Distinguish fundamental quantities from derived quantities
Express a derived unit in terms of base SI units
Convert between multiples and submultiples using SI prefixes

subtopics.name: Measuring Instruments
subtopics.summary: Choosing the right instrument and reading metre rules, vernier callipers and micrometer screw gauges.

objectives.text: Select an appropriate instrument for a given measurement
Read a vernier calliper and a micrometer screw gauge
State the precision of common laboratory instruments

subtopics.name: Errors and Precision
subtopics.summary: Systematic and random error, accuracy versus precision, significant figures and percentage error.

objectives.text: Distinguish systematic error from random error
Distinguish accuracy from precision
Calculate percentage error in a measurement
Report an answer to an appropriate number of significant figures

topics.name: Motion
topics.summary: Describing and predicting how objects move, from straight-line motion to projectiles and Newton's laws.

subtopics.name: Linear Motion
subtopics.summary: Distance, displacement, speed, velocity, acceleration and the equations of uniformly accelerated motion.

objectives.text: Distinguish distance from displacement and speed from velocity
Calculate acceleration from a change in velocity
Apply the equations of uniformly accelerated motion
Solve problems on free fall using g = 10 m/s squared

subtopics.name: Motion Graphs
subtopics.summary: Reading displacement-time and velocity-time graphs, using gradient and area under the graph.

objectives.text: Interpret the gradient of a displacement-time graph as velocity
Interpret the gradient of a velocity-time graph as acceleration
Find distance travelled from the area under a velocity-time graph

subtopics.name: Newton's Laws of Motion
subtopics.summary: Inertia, the relationship between force, mass and acceleration, momentum and action-reaction pairs.

objectives.text: State Newton's three laws of motion
Apply F = ma to solve problems involving resultant force
Calculate momentum and impulse and apply conservation of momentum
Identify action-reaction pairs in everyday situations

subtopics.name: Projectile Motion
subtopics.summary: Treating horizontal and vertical motion independently to find time of flight, range and maximum height.

objectives.text: Explain why horizontal and vertical motion are independent
Calculate time of flight and range for a horizontal projection
Calculate maximum height and range for an inclined projection

topics.name: Forces and Equilibrium
topics.summary: Adding forces, turning effects, and the conditions under which a body stays at rest.

subtopics.name: Equilibrium of Forces
subtopics.summary: Resultant and equilibrant forces, resolution into components and the conditions for equilibrium.

objectives.text: Find the resultant of two or more coplanar forces
Resolve a force into perpendicular components
State and apply the two conditions for equilibrium

subtopics.name: Moments and Levers
subtopics.summary: The turning effect of a force, the principle of moments and how levers multiply effort.

objectives.text: Define moment of a force and state its SI unit
Apply the principle of moments to a balanced beam
Classify levers and identify effort, load and fulcrum

subtopics.name: Centre of Gravity and Stability
subtopics.summary: Locating the centre of gravity and explaining why some objects topple more easily than others.

objectives.text: Define centre of gravity and centre of mass
Describe how to locate the centre of gravity of a lamina
Explain stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium

topics.name: Work, Energy and Power
topics.summary: Energy transfer by forces, conservation of energy, rate of doing work and the efficiency of machines.

subtopics.name: Work and Energy
subtopics.summary: Calculating work done by a force and applying conservation of mechanical energy.

objectives.text: Define work and calculate it as force times distance moved
Calculate kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy
Apply the principle of conservation of mechanical energy

subtopics.name: Power and Efficiency
subtopics.summary: Power as the rate of energy transfer, and why no real machine is 100 per cent efficient.

objectives.text: Define power and state its SI unit
Calculate power from work done and time taken
Calculate efficiency as useful output over total input

subtopics.name: Simple Machines
subtopics.summary: Levers, pulleys and inclined planes, and the link between mechanical advantage, velocity ratio and efficiency.

objectives.text: Define mechanical advantage and velocity ratio
Relate efficiency to mechanical advantage and velocity ratio
Solve problems on pulley systems and inclined planes

topics.name: Heat and Thermal Physics
topics.summary: Temperature and its measurement, heat capacity, changes of state and the behaviour of gases.

subtopics.name: Temperature and Thermometers
subtopics.summary: Temperature as a measure of hotness, thermometric properties, fixed points and scale conversion.

objectives.text: Distinguish heat from temperature
Describe thermometric properties used in thermometers
Convert between the Celsius and Kelvin scales

subtopics.name: Heat Capacity
subtopics.summary: Heat capacity and specific heat capacity, and calculations on heating and mixing.

objectives.text: Define heat capacity and specific heat capacity with units
Apply Q = mc times change in temperature to solve problems
Use the method of mixtures to find a final temperature

subtopics.name: Latent Heat and Change of State
subtopics.summary: Why temperature stays constant during melting and boiling, and latent heat calculations.

objectives.text: Define specific latent heat of fusion and of vaporisation
Explain why temperature is constant during a change of state
Apply Q = ml to solve latent heat problems

subtopics.name: Gas Laws
subtopics.summary: Boyle's law, Charles's law, the pressure law and the general gas equation.

objectives.text: State Boyle's law, Charles's law and the pressure law
Apply the general gas equation to solve problems
Explain why absolute temperature must be used in gas calculations

topics.name: Waves and Sound
topics.summary: How waves carry energy, the wave equation, wave behaviour and the properties of sound.

subtopics.name: Wave Properties
subtopics.summary: Wavelength, frequency, period, amplitude and the wave equation for transverse and longitudinal waves.

objectives.text: Define wavelength, frequency, period and amplitude
Distinguish transverse from longitudinal waves
Apply the wave equation v = f times lambda

subtopics.name: Wave Behaviour
subtopics.summary: Reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference and standing waves.

objectives.text: Describe reflection and refraction of waves
Explain diffraction and the conditions that make it obvious
Explain constructive and destructive interference

subtopics.name: Sound Waves
subtopics.summary: Production and transmission of sound, echoes, pitch and loudness, and resonance in air columns.

objectives.text: Explain how sound is produced and transmitted
Solve problems on echoes and the speed of sound
Relate pitch to frequency and loudness to amplitude
Calculate frequencies of resonance in pipes and strings

topics.name: Light and Optics
topics.summary: Rectilinear propagation of light, reflection at mirrors, refraction and image formation by lenses.

subtopics.name: Reflection and Mirrors
subtopics.summary: The laws of reflection, images in plane mirrors and image formation by curved mirrors.

objectives.text: State and apply the laws of reflection
Describe the image formed by a plane mirror
Apply the mirror formula to curved mirrors

subtopics.name: Refraction of Light
subtopics.summary: Snell's law, refractive index, total internal reflection and real versus apparent depth.

objectives.text: State Snell's law and define refractive index
Calculate the critical angle for a given medium
Relate refractive index to real and apparent depth

subtopics.name: Lenses
subtopics.summary: Converging and diverging lenses, the lens formula, magnification and power of a lens.

objectives.text: Distinguish converging from diverging lenses
Apply the lens formula and the magnification formula
Calculate the power of a lens in dioptres

topics.name: Electricity
topics.summary: Static charge, current and potential difference, Ohm's law, resistor networks and electrical power.

subtopics.name: Electrostatics
subtopics.summary: Charging by friction, induction and contact, Coulomb's law and the electric field.

objectives.text: Describe charging by friction, contact and induction
State and apply Coulomb's law
Define electric field intensity and electric potential

subtopics.name: Current and Ohm's Law
subtopics.summary: Electric current as rate of flow of charge, potential difference, resistance and Ohm's law.

objectives.text: Define electric current and apply Q = It
State Ohm's law and apply V = IR
Relate resistance to length, area and resistivity

subtopics.name: Resistor Networks
subtopics.summary: Series and parallel combinations, current sharing, and internal resistance of a cell.

objectives.text: Calculate effective resistance in series and in parallel
Determine current and potential difference in each branch
Apply E = I times R plus r for a cell with internal resistance

subtopics.name: Electrical Energy and Power
subtopics.summary: Electrical power formulas, energy consumption in kilowatt-hours and the cost of electricity.

objectives.text: Apply the electrical power formulas P = IV, P = I squared R and P = V squared over R
Calculate electrical energy in joules and in kilowatt-hours
Calculate the cost of electricity consumed

topics.name: Magnetism and Electromagnetism
topics.summary: Magnetic fields, the motor effect, induced e.m.f. and how transformers change voltage.

subtopics.name: Magnetic Fields and Forces
subtopics.summary: Magnetic field patterns, fields around current-carrying conductors and the force on a conductor.

objectives.text: Describe magnetic field patterns of magnets and conductors
Apply the right-hand grip rule and Fleming's left-hand rule
Calculate the force on a current-carrying conductor in a field

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic Induction
subtopics.summary: Faraday's and Lenz's laws, factors affecting induced e.m.f. and how a generator works.

objectives.text: State Faraday's laws and Lenz's law of induction
List the factors that affect the size of an induced e.m.f.
Explain the action of a simple a.c. generator

subtopics.name: Transformers
subtopics.summary: The transformer equation, power losses and why electricity is transmitted at high voltage.

objectives.text: Apply the transformer equation to find turns or voltage
Describe energy losses in a transformer and how they are reduced
Explain why power is transmitted at high voltage

topics.name: Modern Physics
topics.summary: The structure of the atom, energy levels, radioactivity and the basics of electronics.

subtopics.name: Atomic Structure and Energy Levels
subtopics.summary: The nuclear model of the atom, energy levels, photons, and the photoelectric effect.

objectives.text: Describe the nuclear model of the atom and define nucleon number
Explain line spectra in terms of energy levels
Apply E = hf and the photoelectric equation

subtopics.name: Radioactivity and Half-Life
subtopics.summary: Alpha, beta and gamma emissions, nuclear equations, half-life and radiation safety.

objectives.text: Compare the properties of alpha, beta and gamma radiation
Balance nuclear equations for radioactive decay
Solve half-life problems
State precautions for handling radioactive sources

subtopics.name: Basic Electronics
subtopics.summary: Conductors, semiconductors and insulators, doping, diodes and rectification.

objectives.text: Distinguish conductors, semiconductors and insulators
Explain n-type and p-type doping
Describe the action of a p-n junction diode in rectification

sources.title: WAEC Physics Syllabus — Senior School Certificate Examination

provenance.note: Topic and subtopic tree mapped to the WAEC/NECO/JAMB Physics syllabus areas, with g = 10 m/s^2 used throughout as the WAEC convention.
